# API Routes

Reading data in Blade happens through the `use` hook in layouts and pages. Writing data happens through the `useMutation` hook in interactive components. Because all client-to-server communication flows through mutations, you don't need to write REST APIs for your own application's UI.

The only reason to expose a REST API is when an external client — an iOS app, a third-party integration, or a webhook consumer — needs to access your data.

## Auto-generated REST API

Blade automatically generates a REST API at `/api` for any models you choose to expose. The request schema is derived from your Triggers, so no extra work is needed beyond defining the trigger and enabling the REST surface in your model definition.

## Custom API routes with Hono

For edge cases where you need a specific request signature that Blade's auto-generated API doesn't cover, create a `router.ts` file at the root of your project and export a [Hono](https://hono.dev) app:

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono';

const app = new Hono()
  .post('/some-path', (c) => c.text('Hello from custom route'));

export default app;
```

Blade mounts this Hono app alongside your application on the same domain. Note that routes defined here cannot interface with the rest of your Blade app — they have no access to the Blade query system or data layer. Think of it as a separate app sharing a domain.

> **Note:** Use the auto-generated REST surface whenever possible. The custom Hono router is for situations where you have no alternative, such as implementing a webhook receiver with a specific payload shape.

## Next steps

See Triggers to add the server-side logic that powers your REST API, or [TypeScript Client](/docs/pages/client) to query RONIN directly from outside a Blade app.
